provenance.pins: datasheet p.3 PIN table (MSOP-10); thermal pad is DFN-only

designVerdict: SELECTED - hot-swap controller, one per channel (U10, U11). Replaces four failed discrete gate networks.
notes: Tokmas second-source LM5069MMX-2, not TI silicon. Live stock 105 at the time of selection, where jlcsearch claimed 2952 - the exact staleness the workflow warns about. CORRECTION: this is the -2 suffix, which AUTO-RESTARTS (datasheet p.13: the Timer pin cycles between 3.6 V and 0.8 V seven times after a fault timeout, 0.5% duty). TI's LM5069MM-1/NOPB (C486026, 89 units, $5.90) is the LATCH-OFF variant. An earlier note here had the two suffixes exactly backwards.

VIN absolute 108 V, operating 8-90 V (p.1, p.5). At 36 V that is 3x margin - the widest of any part on the bus. Below 8 V it holds the gate down, so the channels are off through the whole 5 V pre-negotiation phase with no firmware involvement.
Drives an N-channel FET with a charge pump holding GATE ~12 V above OUT (p.3, pin 10). This is what removes the high-side P-FET gate problem entirely: no level shifters, no Vgs clamp Zeners.

Design values, per channel: R_SENSE 12 mOhm (current limit 55 mV/Rs = 4.58 A typ, 4.0-5.42 A over the 48-65 mV spread), R_PWR 32.4 kOhm (P_LIM ~18 W via Eq. 14), C_TIMER 10 uF X7R 25 V (t_FLT 514 ms via Eq. 11, against t_start 132 ms via Eq. 10), UVLO/OVLO string 120 k / 5.11 k / 7.68 k.

OVLO gives back a hardware overvoltage trip that the HUSB238A lost to its clamp topology - but its +/-10% threshold tolerance is wider than the window between the 37.8 V maximum bus and the modules 45 V absolute, so it cannot be set to protect the modules. Set at 43.2 V nominal to protect the controller.

UVLO doubles as ENABLE: pulling it below 2.5 V disables the channel. A 2N7002 drain on UVLO with a 100 kOhm gate pull-up to 3V3 gives fail-safe-off through MCU reset, and lets the FAULT interlock act on the same node without contending with a driven GPIO.
MSOP-10 RthJA is 156 C/W (p.1), which sounds alarming and is not: IQ is 650 uA max at 37.8 V, about 25 mW.

Design values corrected after review: R_SENSE 10 mOhm not 12 - the current limit must clear the 4.0 A white-flash peak, not the 2.43 A sustained figure, and 12 mOhm put the worst-case trip at exactly 4.0 A. R_PWR 64.9 kOhm gives P_LIM 39.8 W; C_TIMER 6.8 uF; string 120k/5.36k/7.32k.

THE TIMER PIN HAS TWO JOBS. p.3 pin 6 sets the insertion time delay as well as the fault timeout, and p.13 holds GATE down through the insertion time 'regardless of the voltage at VIN or UVLO'. The ratio is fixed at 17.5:1 by the datasheet currents (4 uA insertion, 70 uA fault), so 6.8 uF means a 6.1 s typical hold-off at power-on. Sizing C_TIMER from the fault timeout alone, as the first pass did, silently buys a multi-second delay.
Threshold margins must carry the 1% resistor tolerance, not just the +/-10% comparator spread: on the first divider the stated 1.1 V of OVLO margin was really 0.4 V once the resistors were included.

With C_TIMER 6.8 uF a persistent channel fault retries roughly every 53 s (seven restart cycles at 2.5 uA between 3.6 V and 0.8 V). Firmware can force an earlier retry by toggling the enable GPIO through UVLO.
